An attacker can use this difference to enumerate valid accounts. They can then target those accounts with credential stuffing or phishing. The old code returned one generic error for both cases. The usual fix is to keep that single response. Also consider running a dummy hash check for unknown users so the response time does not leak the same information.
findings.evidence: raise AppError(401, "unknown_email", "No account uses that email")
findings.suggestion: raise AppError(401, "invalid_credentials", "Email or password is incorrect")

judge.rationale: The comment points out that unknown emails now return a distinct `unknown_email` code while wrong passwords return `invalid_credentials`, which enables user enumeration. That is exactly the seeded defect.

findings.label: issue
findings.subject: Session JWT cookie is now readable by JavaScript (httponly disabled)
findings.discussion: With httponly=False, any XSS on the origin can read the session token from document.cookie and steal the session. That token is usable until the JWT TTL expires, so the attacker can replay it from anywhere. The PR gives no reason for the change. If the frontend needs the token, it already gets access_token in the login response body.

judge.rationale: The comment points out that setting httponly=False makes the session cookie readable from JavaScript, which lets an XSS attack steal the session token. That is exactly the seeded defect.

findings.label: issue
findings.subject: Logout no longer clears the session cookie, so users stay authenticated after logging out.
findings.discussion: The `delete_cookie` call was replaced instead of supplemented. The httponly session cookie survives logout and stays valid until the JWT TTL expires. Anyone using the browser afterward (for example on a shared machine) remains logged in. This is a security regression.

judge.rationale: The comment says logout no longer deletes the session cookie, so users stay authenticated, because the delete_cookie call was replaced. That is exactly the seeded defect.

findings.label: issue
findings.subject: Client-facing error code renamed from `not_authenticated` to `unauthorized` without explanation.
findings.discussion: The error code is part of the API contract. Frontends or other clients may branch on `not_authenticated` (for example, to redirect to sign-in), and tests may assert on it. This silent rename can break those consumers. The PR title "Update deps" doesn't describe the change, and no client or test updates come with it.

judge.rationale: The comment flags that the missing-token error code changed from `not_authenticated` to `unauthorized`. It explains this breaks clients and tests that depend on `not_authenticated`, which is the seeded defect.

findings.subject: Tenant name is populated with the tenant id
findings.discussion: `TenantOut.name` is set from `tenant.id` instead of `tenant.name`. Every login and `/me` response will show the tenant id where its display name should be. This is a user-visible regression from the previous `model_validate`, which mapped `name` correctly.
